deep.confirm.title: Run deep care?
deep.confirm.text:
This will:
- clean temporary files and caches
- check the Windows image and repair it if needed
- check and repair system files (sfc /scannow)
- remove old update files
- scan the system drive and trim SSDs
- verify the network connection

It takes 10-20 minutes. You can keep using your PC. Your settings, the Recycle Bin, thumbnails and graphics caches are not touched.
deep.running: Running deep care... this can take a while
health.title: System health
health.sub: Check first, repair only when needed. Checks only read your disk - reading does not wear out SSDs.
health.check.desc: Reads the Windows corruption flag. Instant.
health.scan.desc: Scans the Windows component store for damage. 5-15 minutes.
health.scan.ok: Scan finished. The component store is healthy.
health.repair.desc: Fixes the component store using Windows Update (DISM RestoreHealth). 5-20 minutes.
health.repair.bad: Repair failed (code {0}). An internet connection may be required.
health.sfc.desc: Verifies protected Windows files and restores damaged ones. Run Repair Windows image first if that check failed. 3-10 minutes.
health.sfc.ok: All protected system files are intact.
health.apps.desc: Checks installed apps for newer versions with winget. Outdated apps are the most common security risk.
health.apps.some: {0} app(s) can be updated. Run "winget upgrade --all" to update them.
health.apps.none: All apps are up to date.
health.apps.timeout: The check took too long and was skipped.
health.apps.nowinget: winget is not available on this PC.
health.comp.desc: Deletes Windows components that newer updates replaced. Installed updates can still be uninstalled afterwards. Several minutes.
repair.confirm.title: Repair the Windows image?
repair.confirm.text: DISM will download healthy files from Windows Update if needed. This can take up to 20 minutes.
comp.confirm.title: Remove old update files?
comp.confirm.text: Windows components replaced by newer updates will be deleted. Installed updates stay uninstallable. This takes several minutes.

disks.sub: Free space, drive health and maintenance.
disk.warn.errors: {0} uncorrected read/write errors - back up your data
disk.warn.wear: Wear at {0}% - nearing end of life
disks.fs.desc: Online and read-only scan of the system drive. No restart needed.
disks.fs.bad: A repair record was found. This is usually not a hardware problem. Schedule a quick fix to clear it.
disks.fs.fail: The scan could not be completed.
disks.fs.scheduled: Fix scheduled. Use Restart (not Shut down) to run it.
disks.opt.desc: SSDs only get TRIM, which causes no wear. SSDs are never defragmented.
disks.opt.last: Windows last optimized your drives on {0} ({1} day(s) ago). It does this weekly on its own.
disks.opt.done: Done: {0} SSD(s) trimmed, {1} hard disk(s) defragmented.
spotfix.confirm.title: Schedule a file system fix?
spotfix.confirm.text:
A targeted fix (spot fix) will run at the next start and takes seconds.

Important: use Restart, not Shut down. Fast Startup can skip the fix.
net.title: Network
net.sub: Diagnose connection problems. Only Network reset changes your settings - everything else is safe.
net.dns.desc: Fixes sites that do not load after an address change.
net.adapter.desc: Same as disabling and re-enabling the adapter. Fixes adapters that fail to get an IP after startup.
adapter.confirm.title: Restart the network adapter?
adapter.confirm.text: Your connection will drop for a few seconds. Your settings will not change.

health.sec.repair.desc: Use these when a check reports a problem.
health.sec.updates.desc: Free the space taken by updates that have been replaced by newer ones.

health.verify.desc: Checks protected Windows files without changing anything. 3-10 minutes.
health.verify.ok: All protected system files are intact.
health.verify.bad: Problems found (code {0}). Use Repair system files below.
health.wmi.desc: WMI is used by Windows and many apps to read system information. A damaged repository causes errors in Settings, Task Manager and installers.
health.wmi.bad: The WMI repository is inconsistent (code {0}). Use Repair WMI repository below.
health.scanfile.desc: Checks one protected Windows file and restores it if it is damaged.
health.wmifix.desc: Rebuilds an inconsistent repository and keeps all consistent data.
health.boot.desc: These repair tools only work in the Windows Recovery Environment, not while Windows is running. Your PC uses {0} firmware. Restart into recovery, open Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Command Prompt and type:
health.boot.note: In recovery the Windows drive often has a different letter (for example D:). Check it with "dir D:\Windows" first.
disks.chk.desc: Repairs file system errors. The system drive is checked at the next restart.
disks.chk.r: /r  -  Also locate bad sectors (reads the whole drive, can take hours)
disks.chk.frx: /f /r /x  -  Same, and force the drive offline first
net.advanced.desc: Only if you have connection problems that nothing else fixes. Both reset settings and need a restart.
net.winsock.desc: Resets the Windows network socket catalog. Removes VPN and proxy components that hooked into it.
net.ipreset.desc: Resets TCP/IP to defaults. Manually set IP addresses and DNS servers are lost.

msg.netreset.ok: Reset complete. Restart to apply it.
wmifix.confirm.title: Repair the WMI repository?
wmifix.confirm.text: An inconsistent WMI repository will be rebuilt. Consistent data is kept. Use this only if the check reported a problem.

chkdsk.confirm.system:
{0}

The system drive is in use, so the check will run at the next restart, before Windows starts. Use Restart, not Shut down.
chkdsk.confirm.data:
{0}

chkdsk.confirm.slow: Bad sector scan reads every sector of the drive and can take several hours on large disks.
